test_title: PYST 74: SSC GD Constable - English (Held On - 28 Feb, 2024 Shift 4)
subject: english
question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required’ if the sentence is correct as given.

I got round into the High-street again, (a tiny after that pitfall), and felt myself in comparative security.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the phrase "**a tiny after that pitfall**," which is incorrect.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**a little beyond that pitfall**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in the bracketed word segment of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I got round into the High-street again, **a little beyond that pitfall**, and felt myself in comparative security."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "a little beyond those pitfall" **– This option is incorrect because "those pitfall" is grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 2: "some more besides the pitfall"** – This option is incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4: "No correction required"** – This option is incorrect because the original sentence has a grammatical error.
